article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Indica-leaning hybrid
Genetics: Animal Face × Sin Mintz
Breeder: Ronin Seeds
THC Content: 25-30%
CBD Content: Typically below 1%
Terpene Profile: Caryophyllene , myrcene , limonene
Primary Flavors: Gas, mint, pepper, citrus, cookie dough
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: late September to early October
Indoor Yield: Moderate to high
Outdoor Yield: Moderate to high
Grow Difficulty: Intermediate to advanced

Some marijuana strains make their reputation through a famous parent, while others become desirable because one exceptional plant emerges from a much larger hunt. Frog Poison belongs firmly in the second category. Closely connected with the cultivar better known as Toad Venom and the original keeper nicknamed “Becky,” this modern hybrid combines Animal Face with Sin Mintz to create an unusually aggressive mixture of fuel, mint, pepper, sweet dough, citrus, and fruit. The plant’s visual appeal can be equally dramatic: compact flowers frequently develop dark green and purple shading beneath thick, pale trichome coverage, giving mature buds an almost powdered appearance.

The name deserves clarification because several versions of “Frog Poison” have circulated through the cannabis market. The genetics discussed here are the authentic Animal Face × Sin Mintz family associated with Ronin Seeds and West Coast Connoisseurs. Ronin’s own social activity continues to identify Toad Venom as Animal Face × Sin Mintz, and licensed Ronin nursery material describes the cross more specifically as Animal Face × ( Sin Mint Cookies × Z). Frog Poison is therefore best understood as a market or cut-specific name connected with this genetic line rather than an unrelated strain.
Genetics and Lineage

Animal Face supplies a formidable half of the pedigree. Created from Face Off OG and Animal Mints genetics, the parent carries the resin production, OG-influenced fuel, pine, earth, and penetrating potency that made it valuable to modern breeders. In Frog Poison, those characteristics can appear as dense flowers with sharp gasoline aromas and a cerebral intensity that develops quickly after consumption. Animal Face also helps explain why the finished weed often smells considerably more aggressive than its sweeter secondary notes might suggest.

Sin Mintz provides the contrasting side of the cross. Current licensed Ronin material lists the parent as descending from Sin Mint Cookies and Z genetics, adding mint, confectionery sweetness, fruit, and cookie-like depth to Animal Face’s fuel-heavy foundation. The most famous plant from the resulting population was selected by Green Dragon and originally called Becky before becoming widely associated with Toad Venom. Accounts of the selection consistently describe it as the standout keeper from a relatively small population, which is important because much of Frog Poison’s reputation relates to that particular expression rather than every possible seed phenotype.
Effects and Experience

The first stage tends to announce itself mentally. Rather than beginning with immediate couch-lock, the cannabis can produce a rapid increase in awareness accompanied by euphoria, sharpened sensory perception, and a somewhat energized or creative state. Conversation may become easier, music more immersive, and ordinary surroundings noticeably more interesting. That initial brightness makes the experience surprisingly lively for weed that is often classified as indica leaning.

Physical weight gradually becomes more noticeable as the session matures. Shoulders loosen, muscular tension can fade into the background, and the energetic edge settles into a calmer mental state. With moderate consumption, that progression can create an appealing balance between cerebral engagement and physical relaxation. Larger amounts are a different matter. Potent batches may produce heavy eyelids, slowed coordination, short-term memory disruption, and prolonged sedation. Contemporary examples of this genetic family frequently reach the upper commercial potency range, with some laboratory-tested products exceeding 30% total THC, making conservative dosing sensible for inexperienced consumers.
Medical Benefits

No controlled clinical trials have evaluated Frog Poison as a distinct medical marijuana cultivar, so therapeutic claims should not be treated as established medical outcomes. Nevertheless, its combination of strong THC activity and progressively relaxing effects may explain why some medical cannabis consumers gravitate toward similar chemotypes for temporary relief from discomfort, appetite loss, stress, or difficulty settling down during the evening. The euphoric opening may also appeal to patients who dislike cultivars that become immediately lethargic.

Its high potency also creates limitations. THC can worsen anxiety, dizziness, rapid heartbeat, cognitive impairment, or paranoia in susceptible people, particularly when doses are increased rapidly. Anyone using cannabis alongside prescription medication or for a significant medical condition should discuss cannabinoid use with an appropriate healthcare professional. Strain names are not reliable substitutes for chemistry; medical consumers will gain more useful information from the cannabinoid and terpene certificate for the specific batch they intend to use.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Frog Poison earns its name with an aroma that is considerably stranger than a straightforward sweet or fruity hybrid. Freshly opened flower can produce an immediate rush of gasoline, pepper, cool mint, and pungent earth. After several seconds, sweeter material begins pushing through: citrus peel, cookie dough, tart candy, and occasionally peach or tropical fruit. Some expressions lean almost chemical, blending fuel and mint into an aroma reminiscent of solvent, menthol, and sweet pastry.

Breaking the flowers apart usually exposes the heavier side of the profile. Warm spice and damp earth become stronger while the sugary notes recede, suggesting meaningful caryophyllene and myrcene influence. Pinene can contribute an herbal sharpness, while limonene-heavy examples develop brighter citrus edges. On the palate, gas and pepper often arrive first, followed by mint-cookie sweetness before an earthy, slightly fruity finish remains after the exhale. Different growers can push the profile substantially in one direction or another, which is why authenticated genetics and a careful cure matter so much with this cultivar.
Growing Information

This plant is better suited to growers with some experience controlling vigorous modern hybrids. Indoor cultivation commonly falls near an eight-to-nine-week flowering window, although phenotype and environmental conditions can shift maturity. Dense branching responds well to early shaping, topping, and selective pruning, particularly when growers want to create an even canopy beneath artificial lighting. Stretch is usually manageable rather than extreme, but sufficient space between flowering sites helps light penetration and reduces trapped humidity.

Late bloom is where environmental discipline becomes particularly important. Heavy resin coverage and compact flowers can retain moisture, so strong air movement and controlled humidity help protect dense colas as harvest approaches. The plant should receive adequate structural support once flower weight increases. Outdoors, a warm season followed by a relatively dry early autumn is preferable, with late September into early October serving as a reasonable harvest range in many Northern Hemisphere environments. Growers selecting from multiple plants should pay close attention to aroma and resin rather than yield alone; the most desirable keeper may be the individual displaying the piercing mint-gas-funk character associated with the famous cut.
FAQ
What strain is Frog Poison?

Frog Poison is an indica-leaning hybrid associated with the Animal Face × Sin Mintz genetics bred by Ronin Seeds/West Coast Connoisseurs. The genetic family is most famous under the Toad Venom name, with the original standout keeper having been called Becky.
Is Frog Poison the same as Toad Venom?

In the context of the authentic Animal Face × Sin Mintz cut, Frog Poison is commonly used as an alternate or market-specific name associated with Toad Venom. Because unrelated flower can be sold under popular strain names, consumers should verify the producer and lineage rather than relying on the name alone.
What does Frog Poison taste like?

The flavor is dominated by gas, cool mint, pepper, earthy cookie dough, citrus, and sweet fruit. Certain batches become especially fuel-heavy, while others emphasize tart candy, creamy dough, or fruity Z-influenced sweetness.
How strong is Frog Poison?

It should be considered a high-potency marijuana strain. Modern examples of the Toad Venom/Frog Poison genetic family frequently appear in the mid-20% to low-30% THC range, with individual laboratory-tested batches sometimes exceeding that level. Actual potency should always be taken from the batch certificate rather than a generic strain percentage.
Is Frog Poison indica or sativa?

The cultivar is a hybrid commonly treated as indica leaning. Its effects are less straightforward than that classification suggests, however, because the early phase can feel mentally energetic and euphoric before stronger body relaxation develops later.
Final Thoughts on Frog Poison

Frog Poison represents the kind of modern cannabis cultivar whose reputation depends as much on selection as pedigree. Animal Face establishes a potent foundation of gas, resin, earth, and intensity, while Sin Mintz introduces mint, cookie sweetness, citrus, and fruit. The famous keeper pulled those traits together in an unusually loud package, producing marijuana capable of smelling simultaneously sweet, chemical, spicy, and fuel-soaked.

Its appeal extends beyond potency. The staged effects, dense trichome production, dark visual character, and unusually complicated aroma give the strain enough individuality to stand apart in a market crowded with high-THC hybrids. Growers should be particularly careful about provenance because the Frog Poison and Toad Venom names have been applied inconsistently as demand has grown. When the genetics trace back to the authentic Animal Face × Sin Mintz line, however, this weed offers a distinctive example of contemporary boutique breeding built around an exceptional keeper rather than a name alone.
